title: Matrix Fact for Fast Multi-dimensional Slicing and Cohort Heatmaps in Console Analytics
creator: Marina Patel
description: Motivation: ad-hoc Console dashboards and internal Power BI queries frequently need fast multi-dimensional slicing (workspace x route x model x time x user_tier) and cohort heatmaps for adoption analysis. Current event-level stores and broad rollup tables either return slow queries for wide slices or require expensive on-the-fly aggregation. Proposal: build a compressed sparse 'matrix_fact' curated table that pre-aggregates counts and basic metrics at multiple granularities and stores them in a layout optimized for high-cardinality slicing with small scan sizes.
schema_notes: Primary shape: matrix_fact_v1 (date_bucket, workspace_id, route_id, model_id, user_tier, metric_id, value) with metric_id enum (requests, unique_users, tokens, errors)
Store as Parquet with columnar encoding + dictionary encoding for id columns; use delta encoding for integers and run-length for sparse runs
Use surrogate integer IDs for route_id/model_id/user_tier to reduce string cardinality; maintain mapping tables in curated dimension schemas
Include shard_id and compressed_bucket for extremely wide workspaces to enable targeted reads
Expose a 'matrix_view' materialized view that expands metric_id into columns for BI compatibility when needed
partitioning_and_retention: Partition by date_bucket (daily) and dataset_namespace (prod|staging) to allow efficient time range scans
Subpartition by workspace_id hash into 256 buckets for very large customers to avoid single-partition hotspots
Retention policy: keep full daily buckets for 365 days, roll up to weekly aggregates for 2 years, and purge per-customer if requested by compliance
Backfill plan will create temporary intermediate partitions and then compact into canonical buckets to avoid double-counting
etl_plan: Ingest from console-event-stream consumer 'analytics-raw' and existing curated route_activity tables
Map events to canonical keys using dim mappings service job (job_dim_mappings_v2) to ensure consistent ids
Compute incremental deltas every 10 minutes producing micro-batches which are merged to daily matrix_fact partitions using idempotent upserts
Weekly compaction job to merge micro-batches and rebuild dictionary encoding; scheduled as job_analytics_matrix_compact_v1
Backfill strategy: staged compute starting from last known consistent snapshot plus replayed Kafka offsets; use job_matrix_backfill_18234
Expose a small set of aggregate materialized views for common slices (workspace-week-route) with auto-refresh window
perf_targets: Ad-hoc BI queries that slice a typical dashboard (<= 10 dimensions, one workspace) should complete under 3 seconds 95% of the time
Large multi-workspace intersects (e.g., corporate rollups across 50 workspaces) should complete under 25 seconds with streaming prefetch
Daily ETL ingest latency: micro-batches visible in matrix_fact within 15 minutes
Storage per 1M daily events projected <= 1.2GB after compression using sparse encoding
acceptance_criteria: matrix_fact_v1 schema deployed in curated analytics dataset with correct partitioning and docs
Incremental ETL runs for at least 7 days without data correctness incidents and with metrics for ingestion latency and duplicate suppression
Representative BI dashboards (console adoption, route heatmap) backed by matrix_fact_v1 meet perf targets on staging cluster
Backfill for last 90 days completes and reconciles to known gold counts within 0.5% for sample workspaces
Mapping tables and transformation logic reviewed and merged (PR linked), and runbooks added to Confluence
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: cardinality explosion if we pre-aggregate too fine-grained dimensions. Mitigation: limit metric_id and use surrogate ids; offer optional 'wide' namespace for opt-in customers
Risk: expensive compaction CPU cost causing ETL throttling. Mitigation: schedule compactions off-peak and use autoscaling compute pools with cost cap alerts
Risk: schema evolution and BI breakage when metric_id expands. Mitigation: maintain stable metric enum and migration path using materialized views
Risk: query semantics mismatch for edge cases (deduped users vs raw events). Mitigation: provide audit queries and reconciliation dashboards
